method: Every expectation was written from the sources in src/ by reading them; no analysis tool was run on the sources or on the built inputs, and no tool's detectors or output were looked at. The three inputs are the same program: packed as written, bundled by esbuild, and bundled and minified. main.js, preload.js and the helper modules shared/ipc.js, shared/endpoints.js, shared/time.js and main/window-options.js are written as tsc emits TypeScript compiled to CommonJS: `const electron_1 = require("electron")` and every Electron call reads electron_1.ipcMain.handle(...), electron_1.contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld(...); constants are `exports.NAME = "..."` and are read as ipc_1.NAME or ipc_1.Channels.Name; default imports go through __importDefault, so electron-store is constructed as `new electron_store_1.default(...)` and node:path is used as node_path_1.default.join; imported functions are called as `(0, window_options_1.windowOptions)(...)`. renderer.js and renderer-mini.js are ES modules (as a Vite build of a renderer would be). Bundling keeps the file names main.js, preload.js, renderer.js and renderer-mini.js and folds the helper modules (and lib/keys.js) into the entry files that use them. Roles and settings are attributed to the four entry files; that is right for the plain input as well, because the helper modules hold constants, option values and formatting functions only: every IPC call, every new BrowserWindow, every exposeInMainWorld, every request and every storage access is written in an entry file. A window setting is attributed to the file that creates the window (main.js), also where its value is written in main/window-options.js. The bundled and minified main.js and preload.js were also run in Node against stand-ins for Electron and electron-store (outside the repository, not kept); the channels registered and invoked, the exposed members and the channels they touch, and the web preferences of the three windows were exactly the ones listed here. Requests and storage of the renderers and the main-to-renderer sends inside handlers were checked by reading. An expectation states what the program does, also where that is hard to see; what only looks like a finding is listed under absent. webPreferences lists the keys preload, contextIsolation, nodeIntegration and sandbox only, one entry per window and key that the code writes (directly or through the defaults of windowOptions()); keys the code does not write are not listed with Electron's defaults. Requests: the renderer talks to the Cadence API through the class ApiClient written in renderer.js; its one fetch is `fetch(`${this.baseUrl}${path}`, ...)`, the single instance is `new ApiClient(API_ROOT)` and every call of get/post/delete passes a literal path or a template that starts with a literal. Each request made through it is listed with the address it really goes to; the fetch inside request() is not counted as unreadable, and API_ROOT alone (https://api.cadence.example/v2) is the known leading part of that fetch but is never requested as such, so it is listed neither as present nor as absent. `audio.src = track.path` in the AudioEngine sets a local file (or an object URL) as the source of the audio element; it is not a request call and is not counted. shell.openExternal(address) hands an address to the operating system; the application requests nothing, so such addresses are absent and the call is not a request call.
